extracted.intended_audience: congressional staff, policymakers, DoD acquisition and procurement officials, and procurement policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and oversight of Department of Defense competitive sourcing, A-76 public-private competitions, and FAIR Act inventory/reporting requirements, including statutory thresholds, procedural roles (e.g., ATO), reporting, and contract management standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core function determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination whether the work activity or function is considered “core” to the mission or component, whether the function has been identified as “inherently governmental” according to OMB Circular A-76 rules, and how the function is coded on FAIRNET (the Web-based guide to DOD’s inventory under the FAIR Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-part consideration noted: (1) is the activity core to mission/component; (2) is it identified as inherently governmental per OMB A-76; (3) how it is coded on FAIRNET. The Business Initiative Council (BIC) was formed to lead identification of what is a core function within DOD; agency coding and public posting on FAIRNET are part of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on conversion to contractor performance (P.L. 108-287)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion to contractor performance of any activity or function in DOD that, as of August 5, 2004, is performed by 11 or more DOD civilian employees is limited unless specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion permitted only if: (1) the conversion is based on a public-private competition involving a Most Efficient Organization (MEO); (2) the MEO’s personnel-related costs are 10% or $10 million less than that of the contractor; and (3) the contractor offers a bid proposal requiring less financial contribution toward the premium share of DOD health benefits for civilian employees compared to that paid by DOD under 5 U.S.C. Chapter 89.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Tender Official (ATO) duties under OMB Circular A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: The ATO shall (1) be an inherently governmental agency official with decision-making authority; (2) comply with the circular; (3) be independent of the contracting officer (CO), source selection authority (SSA), source selection evaluation board (SSEB), and performance work statement (PWS) team; (4) develop, certify, and represent the agency tender; (5) designate the MEO team after public announcement of the standard competition; (6) provide necessary resources and training to prepare a competitive agency tender; and (7) be a directly interested party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency must ensure the ATO has access to available resources (e.g., skilled manpower, funding) necessary to develop a competitive agency tender. Independence from procurement teams and responsibility for certification/representation are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: ATO authority to file protests / 'interested party' status (P.L. 108-375 §326)
rubrics_metrics.description: P.L. 108-375 grants the agency tender official authority to serve as an “interested party” and to file a protest on behalf of federal employees, unless the ATO determines there is no reasonable basis for the protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an interested party files a protest, a person representing a majority of the federal employees engaged in the activities subject to the competition may intervene in the protest. The ATO’s judgment about reasonable basis can prevent filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal cost comparison and cost-savings threshold for conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Public-private conversions require a formal cost comparison and a demonstrated cost-savings of $10 million or 10% before activities performed by federal employees can be converted to private contractor performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 327 (P.L. 108-375) and related provisions require formal cost comparisons during competitions and a cost-savings threshold of either $10 million or 10% to permit conversion. Other statutory language reiterates that conversions of activities performed by more than 10 civilian employees require a certified most-efficient and cost-effective organization plan and a cost differential of 10% or $10,000,000 equal to or less than the personnel-related costs of the MEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and accountability requirements for contractor workforce (P.L. 108-375)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD must provide new accountability on reporting the size and scope of the service contractor workforce; the DOD Inspector General must report to Congress on sufficiency of employees to conduct competitions and on whether DOD has systems to track and assess cost and quality of contractor-performed functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary of Defense required to submit two reports by end of April 2005: (1) guidance on policies for management/oversight of contractors supporting deployed forces (roles/responsibilities of commanders, coordination of contractor security movements, rules of engagement for armed contractor security personnel, categories of functions to determine inherent-governmental status); and (2) policy guidance and a plan to manage contractor personnel (procedures for documenting decisions, disciplinary/criminal actions taken, legal status after sovereignty transfer, and data collection on number/type of contractors, contract value, casualties, and number of contractor personnel in theater).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on offshore outsourcing (JOBS Act amendment S.2660)
rubrics_metrics.description: The JOBS Act amendment would prohibit most federal civilian agencies from procuring goods or services from companies that perform 'offshore outsourcing' (sending jobs overseas), with exceptions for certain agencies and programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions made for agencies such as Defense and Homeland Security and selected Department of Energy programs, and for items unavailable within the United States. The amendment seeks to 'protect United States workers from competition of foreign workforces' in federal and state contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Best value' pilot for IT services (FY2004 Authorization §336)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization for a pilot program to procure information technology services using 'best value' as a source selection criterion in the competitive sourcing process, with an exemption from certain statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Comptroller General is directed to review the pilot program and report to Congress by February 1, 2008. Language exempts the pilot program from the requirements of 10 U.S.C. 2462.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract consolidation / bundling safeguards (§801)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before consolidating contract requirements (contract bundling), the Secretary of Defense and other senior officials must ensure that consolidation provides small businesses with appropriate opportunities and that market research and alternate approaches have been identified and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior acquisition officials must conduct market research, identify alternative contracting approaches, and determine that contract consolidation is necessary and justified before executing an acquisition strategy to consolidate contracts above $5 million. The provision aims to preserve small business opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition requirements for Iraqi reconstruction contracts (§805 and §1442)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD must comply with the Competition in Contracting Act and relevant procurement laws for Iraqi reconstruction contracts and procure through full and open competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1442 requires publication in the Federal Register or Commerce Business Daily of any contracts for repair/maintenance/construction in Iraq that are without full and open competition no later than 30 days after contract entry; some post-September 30, 2005 exclusions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and waivers for procurement from foreign sources (various appropriations provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibitions on procurement of certain defense items/components from foreign countries that restrict sale or provision of military goods/services to the United States; Secretary of Defense may exercise waiver authority with written notification and justification to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2004 and other appropriations include specific buy-American-like prohibitions (e.g., carbon, alloy, or armor steel plating sourcing, welding/manufacture rules for shipboard anchor and mooring chain, Buy American Act compliance/waiver authority and exceptions). Some provisions authorize incentive programs for contractors who buy U.S.-manufactured capital assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and funding restrictions on A-76 cost comparison studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on the use of appropriated funds for A-76 cost comparison studies that exceed statutory timeframes; prohibitions on contracting out unless required analyses and certifications are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions prohibit use of funds to perform an A-76 cost comparison study if the study exceeds 24 months after initiation for a single-function activity or 30 months (in some texts 48 months) for a multi-function activity. Other sections require completion and certification of a 'most efficient and cost-effective analysis' before contracting out activities performed by ten or more civilian employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depot maintenance competition safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits competitions for depot maintenance between DOD and private firms provided senior acquisition officials certify that successful bids include comparable estimates of all direct and indirect costs for both public and private bids; policies governing OMB Circular A-76 may not apply to competitions under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires certification by the DOD Senior Acquisition Executive for the military or the defense agency that successful bids include comparable cost estimates; intended to ensure apples-to-apples comparisons in depot maintenance competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR Act inventory requirements, publication, and agency review
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the FAIR Act, agencies must submit annual inventories of activities considered inherently governmental and those considered not inherently governmental; OMB will review, consult with agency heads, and publish the lists for Congress and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless exempted, OMB guidance requires all executive branch agencies to submit a compliant inventory or a letter indicating all FTEs are inherently governmental. The Director of OMB is required to publish the list in the Federal Register 'within a reasonable time thereafter.' Agency heads must review the activities on the list and consider contracting them out through competitive processes (with noted exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge and appeals process for inventory inclusion/exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies, contractors, and labor unions may file challenges to inclusion or exclusion of activities from agency inventories; upon challenge, agencies must accept, make changes, or reject the challenge within 30 days after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges have been filed against agencies (e.g., NASA) over whether certain positions are commercial or inherently governmental. If unresolved administratively, aggrieved bidders may seek legal remedies; protracted legal challenges can lengthen procurement cycles and trigger additional oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract management and administration quality indicators (GAO / DOD IG findings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit findings identify deficiencies that indicate poor contract management and administration, including non-use of prior history to define requirements, inadequate government cost estimates, cursory technical reviews, inadequate competition, failure to award multiple-award contracts, inadequate price negotiation memoranda, inadequate contract surveillance, and lack of cost control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO/DOD IG statistics cited (e.g., 69% non-use of prior history, 77% inadequate cost estimates, 57% cursory technical reviews, 60% inadequate competition, 68% inadequate price negotiation memos, 67% inadequate contract surveillance) illustrate systemic weaknesses. Results included long-running cost-type contracts without performance measures and 'material weaknesses' in procurement system controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for performance measures to judge efficiency and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts for services often lacked performance measures to judge efficiency and effectiveness of services rendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD IG found instances where cost-type contracts persisted for decades with no performance measures; the lack of such measures undermines oversight and assessment of contractor performance and savings claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for assessing whether outsourcing compromises national security
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating whether to outsource sensitive functions (e.g., weapons handling), consider safety/training standards, risks from strikes or work stoppages, federal employee oaths/loyalty versus contractors, and likelihood that cost/efficiency incentives will replace experienced personnel with less-experienced, lower-paid workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics argue outsourcing certain functions may compromise national security due to lower training/education standards among contractors, inability to prevent strikes, differing allegiance, and cost-driven staffing decisions. These qualitative factors should weigh into outsourcing decisions for mission-critical functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic competition and savings goal setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish realistic competition schedules and savings goals, accounting fully for the costs and time required to run public-private competitions, or risk overstating expected savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO concluded that DOD's estimated savings did not adequately account for the costs of conducting competitions and likely overstated projected savings; competitions often take longer than projected, reducing annual savings. Components often lack detailed plans/analyses to judge practicality of competing the planned number of positions.
